page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Heading at top centred; then running text with a large woodcut initial M at the start of the first paragraph. Page number and catchword-like marks at the foot: "(?) (?) 3" and "Aucto-" at the lower right, which is a catchword.

main_text.head: Syllabus Auctorum, qui Annalibus his operam suam commodârunt.
Manu-scripta.
main_text.p: Manu-scripta, quibus in his Annalibus usus sum, sunt hæc sequentia:

Chronicon Levoldi à Northoff, nobilis Markani, Canonici Leodiensis & Abbatis sæcularis Visetensis, qui sub Eberhardo Comite Marckano vixit, & cum filio ejusdem Engelberto Romam, anno 1326. profectus est. Hoc Chronicon ex Latino barbaro in Westphalicum idioma convertit Ulricus Verne sacellanus Hammonensis: ex Westphalico in Germanicum purius Joannes Kurtz / rationum Camerae Clivensis Magister: Latinitate vero tertiori donavit, notisque suis eruditis illustravit M. Henricus Meibomius Lemgoviensis, poëticês & historiarum Professor in Academia Julia.

Chronicon Gerhardi Schurenij, sive ab Horreo dicti, Sanctensis, Ducum Cliviae Adolphi Victoriosi & Joannis bellicosi secretarius, in quo Principum Clivensium & Marckensium originem atque progressum usque ad annum 1552. deduxit, licet anno 1489. adhuc superstes fuerit. Ab anno vero isto 1452. usque ad annum 1590. Johannes Lowerman Emmericensis, Jurisconsultus & Wilhelmi Cliviae, Juliae, Montium Ducis Consiliarius, inde Ioannes Turcus Gochensis Secretarius & Registrator Clivensis in praesens tempus deduxerunt.

Chronicon aliud, in quo omnium Romanorum Impp. Colon. Ultraject. Monast. Osnaburg. & Paderborn. Episcoporum, omnium item Brabant. Holland. Flandr. Gelr. Cliv. Jul. Mont. Marck. Ducum & Comitum res gestae parallelas descriptae sunt, quod mihi ex Averdorpensi coenobio Vcsallensi communicavit ejus quondam quaestor, vir multae lectionis & antiquitatis in primis patriae studiosus Theodoricus ab Uppich ὁ μαχαιρίτης.
Arnholdus Heimricius Clivensis, Decanus Sanctensis in mss. variis, duobus tomis in Bibliotheca ejusdem Ecclesiae extantibus.

page.notes: Woodcut initial M at the start of the first paragraph. Greek phrase after Uppich is printed in italic. Page number printed as "3" with "(?) (?)" marks to its left, likely signature or printer's marks; transcribed the page number only. Some words in the scan are faint or show-through; "Vcsallensi" and "Visetensis" are uncertain readings. The "Kurtz" line is in black letter.
